claims.statement: The Docker Desktop / Docker-in-Docker devcontainer path is retained solely for Android emulator support via /dev/kvm; all other work (web E2E, integration, agent stack, day-to-day assistant work) runs on the Docker Sandbox microVM primary environment, which measured 0.43× the wall-clock of this path across five stages.

The devcontainer provides two distinct isolation strengths: strong host-filesystem/credential/SSH isolation (no host profile, SSH keys, credential store, or Docker socket mounted) and only moderate container-engine isolation because DinD requires the container to run privileged, accepting a potential escape path to the shared Docker Desktop WSL2 host engine.

init-firewall.sh enforces a default-deny outbound egress policy with a narrow allowlist (Anthropic API, GitHub, npm, container-image registries and their CDN blob hosts) using ipset/iptables; the FORWARD chain is left to dockerd so nested-container networking is not broken, meaning nested containers' egress is not independently firewalled.

Docker Desktop Enhanced Container Isolation (ECI) must remain OFF; ECI is incompatible with the docker-in-docker devcontainer feature and causes a 'mount: /sys/kernel/security: permission denied' failure.

Two VS Code-specific behaviors break a privileged DinD container on Docker Desktop + WSL2: the Wayland-socket bind-mount (fixed by setting dev.containers.mountWaylandSocket: false in VS Code User settings) and the Docker credential-helper injection (already fixed in committed config via containerEnv.DOCKER_CONFIG=/home/coder/.docker-dind).

Host env vars forwarded into the devcontainer via ${localEnv} (MCM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MCM_DEVCONTAINER_IMAGE, FORGE_REGISTRY_HOST, TMDB_API_KEY, MCM_FORGE_TOKEN, MCM_FORGE_ISSUE_TOKEN) are read from the VS Code process environment at launch time; setx alone is not enough — VS Code must be fully quit and relaunched with the value already present, then the container recreated.

MCM_DEVCONTAINER_IMAGE is required under VS Code — the ${localEnv:VAR:default} fallback default is NOT applied by the VS Code Dev Containers extension; with the var unset, VS Code passes --build-arg BASE_IMAGE= (empty) and the build fails. The headless @devcontainers/cli does apply the default.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must never be set directly on the host or in the devcontainer shell; Claude Code silently prefers it over a subscription login. The key is carried as MCM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and remapped to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only at the point of use (agent gateway, OpenWiki maintenance, containerized E2E recipe) — each a separate process running no interactive assistant. Measured 2026-08-16: ~$15 unintended API spend in one day.

api.themoviedb.org is allowlisted in init-firewall.sh for the devcontainer shell's OUTPUT chain (needed by the pytest integration test runner) but runtime app paths (BFF validate-on-save probe, web-api-mcp curator enrichment) run as nested containers traversing the FORWARD chain and never needed the allowlist entry. Conflating the two chains is the documented trap; a stale ruleset causing timeouts should be fixed by re-applying init-firewall.sh, not by widening the allowlist.

crates.io, index.crates.io, and static.crates.io ARE allowlisted in the devcontainer egress firewall (group `packages` in .devcontainer/egress-allowlist.json), so cargo resolves online in the devcontainer; --offline is now a tool, not a requirement. A failing --offline resolve still signals that a change adds a package absent from Cargo.lock and remains a useful lock-discipline check.

getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND keycloak-service when running the integration tier in the devcontainer shell is caused by .env.docker (loaded by tests/integration/setup/env.ts for CI) containing Docker-internal hostnames not overridden for a host-shell run. Fix: export KEYCLOAK_URL=http://localhost:8099, MONGO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27018, REDIS_TEST_URL=redis://localhost:6379/1. Measured 2026-08-09: 84 failed/31 passed without these exports; 114/115 with them.

Local Ollama runs inside the devcontainer via the dev-ollama nested container (scripts/devcontainer-ollama.sh, run at postStartCommand, using infrastructure-as-code/docker/dev-ollama.compose.yaml), publishing on 0.0.0.0:11434 — 0.0.0.0 rather than loopback because a nested container reaches the bridge gateway. The agent gateway already targets host.docker.internal:11434, so it reaches dev-ollama with no gateway change, image rebuild, or firewall change.

The Android SDK and an android-34 google_apis x86_64 system image are baked into the toolchain image; the privileged DinD container passes through the host /dev/kvm, enabling a headless hardware-accelerated emulator boot. An older MCM_DEVCONTAINER_IMAGE silently has no Android layer and devcontainer-android.sh no-ops cleanly rather than erroring.

~/.claude.json (Claude Code's global config holding oauthAccount, userID, machineID, and session history) is a sibling of the ~/.claude directory in $HOME on the ephemeral overlay and was NOT persisted by the mcm-claude volume. Fix: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/coder/.claude in containerEnv relocates the config root onto the volume (item #257, measured 2026-08-27). A symlink does not work because Claude Code replaces the file via write-then-rename, swapping the symlink for a regular overlay file.

Docker won't start after a devcontainer rebuild when a previous container instance is still running; its containerd holds an flock on the DinD volume's meta.db, blocking the new daemon indefinitely. Diagnosis: python3 flock probe distinguishes locked (recoverable) from corrupt (destructive). Fix: docker rm -f every other container, then sudo nohup /usr/local/share/docker-init.sh. Do NOT delete meta.db or docker volume rm — meta.db deletion destroys all DinD images, and /workspaces is a named volume so a prune removes the working tree.

Editing a file under node_modules/ writes into the pnpm content-addressed store because node_modules entries are hardlinks into it; files with identical content share one inode across package versions. A per-file backup-then-patch loop corrupts its own backups (the store entry changes with the first write), and pnpm install does not re-verify store content hashes so corruption outlives a reinstall. Safe procedure: stat -c '%h %i' first, record clean md5sum, patch one path, then verify with md5 and pnpm store status.

Multiple Claude sessions share one devcontainer and one checkout; git operations in /workspaces/mcm are visible to all sessions. Branch work must use a git worktree under /home/coder/worktrees/<slug>. The node_modules symlink from the worktree to the main checkout is sufficient for node --test and scripts/*.mjs gates but causes ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR for any pnpm nx target — a real pnpm install in the worktree is the only fix (~4 min). Worktrees do not survive a container rebuild.
An nx failure message that does not match the state on disk is likely stale cached output; re-run with --skip-nx-cache to get the real error before diagnosing.

The node_modules symlink in a worktree was previously committable because .gitignore carried node_modules/ with a trailing slash (matching only directories, not symlinks); this caused every install-bearing CI job to fail with ENOTDIR. Fixed by changing the pattern to node_modules (no trailing slash).

The devcontainer's egress destination list is no longer inlined in init-firewall.sh: it lives in .devcontainer/egress-allowlist.json as the single canonical list, read through scripts/gen-egress-policy.mjs --format ipset-domains (the same generator that emits the sandbox's host-side policy), with the forge registry host injected at runtime from FORGE_REGISTRY_HOST rather than stored. init-firewall.sh refuses to apply default-deny if the generator is missing, if node is absent from root's PATH, if the generator fails, or if it resolves to zero domains — so a generator crash cannot silently produce a total egress blackout.

The Docker Desktop devcontainer.json still passes its credentials (MCM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, TMDB_API_KEY, MCM_FORGE_TOKEN, MCM_FORGE_ISSUE_TOKEN) through containerEnv, whereas the sandbox variant removed them because the devcontainer CLI compiles every containerEnv entry into an ENV instruction in the generated Dockerfile-with-features — measured 2026-09-19 as literal values in Config.Env and 3 history layers of the derived image, a permanent leak that survives every recreate and is handed out by docker image inspect / docker history. The sandbox path passes them instead with docker run --env-file, generated by .devcontainer/gen-container-secrets-env.sh from the VM env file (remoteEnv is unusable because ssh + docker exec sessions never see it).

Reaching the nested app stacks' published ports from the dev-container shell requires two firewall rules together: the loopback ACCEPT and an egress ACCEPT over the container's own docker bridges (docker0 plus the br-* user-defined bridges, scoped by interface name so bridges created later are covered). The bridge rule is RFC1918-only and opens no internet egress. A published port that goes unreachable after working earlier is a stale ruleset, so the fix is re-applying init-firewall.sh rather than widening the internet allowlist.

The devcontainer lifecycle hooks divide responsibility: onCreateCommand repairs cache and workspace-artifact ownership and seeds Claude Code's config, postCreateCommand runs pnpm install (with --config.confirmModulesPurge=false), and postStartCommand re-applies the default-deny firewall (ipset is not persisted), brings up the nested dev-ollama, and prepares the Android emulator. postStartCommand forwards FORGE_REGISTRY_HOST through `sudo env` because sudo resets the environment, so a plain `sudo bash init-firewall.sh` would silently skip the forge allowlist.

The devcontainer's two-Dockerfile image seam lets the heavy toolchain be prebuilt and pulled per open: .devcontainer/Dockerfile is a thin `FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}` and devcontainer.json feeds BASE_IMAGE from ${localEnv:MCM_DEVCONTAINER_IMAGE}, because top-level `image` is not substitution-eligible but build.args is. The forge host literal stays out of git by living only in the host env, and the local-fallback tag is colon-free because ${localEnv:VAR:default} truncates its default at the first colon (a colon-containing env value, the digest pin, passes through intact).

Behaviour-named verification scripts under .devcontainer/verify/ each assert one devcontainer success criterion and fail rather than self-heal; they span in-container, VM-side and Windows-host vantage points, and the aggregate runner .devcontainer/verify/run-harness.sh enumerates the twelve expected scripts by name so a renamed or lost script fails the run instead of silently shrinking the checked set, counts anything without an explicit pass as a failure, and requires the Windows-side engine-seam proof to be supplied via MCM_HOST_CHECK rather than inventing it.

The MCM_-prefix point-of-use mapping rule extends to the OpenWiki generator's Fireworks credential: MCM_FIREWORKS_API_KEY is mapped to FIREWORKS_API_KEY only inside the generator's own process (scripts/wiki-provider.mjs declares the accepted names and mapTo, and the launcher gives the child only the selected provider's key), and api.fireworks.ai is in the canonical egress allowlist for model traffic only — the fireworks.ai website FQDN is deliberately not covered. Unlike the four older credentials, MCM_FIREWORKS_API_KEY is not in the Docker Desktop path's containerEnv; it travels only on the sandbox path, where .devcontainer/gen-container-secrets-env.sh emits it into the --env-file alongside the four.

.devcontainer/gen-container-secrets-env.sh is the only channel that turns the sandbox's shell-form ~/.mcm-sandbox-env into the bare KEY=value form docker --env-file requires, because --env-file performs no quote processing (measured: Q1='quoted' arrives as Q1=['quoted'], failing auth in a way that reads as a bad key). It guards its own failure modes: the output file is created mode 600 before any write rather than chmodded after, a value containing a newline is refused rather than emitted as a bogus extra entry (using bash's $'\n' — $(printf '\n') evaluates to the empty string and degrades the pattern to match every value), a missing source file yields an empty env file rather than a failed container start, and the summary reports only variable names and lengths, never values.

The thin .devcontainer/Dockerfile layer on top of the prebuilt toolchain image must stay minimal: a layer that changes file metadata (a UID renumber is the tempting one) copies every touched file up into the new overlay layer, so a "thin" renumber duplicated the whole ~13 GB image and the build died in `exporting layers` with `no space left on device` on the Android system image (measured 2026-08-17). The same disk exhaustion is the likeliest cause of a docker-outside-of-docker feature install failing with exit 100, which reads as an apt fault; `updateRemoteUserUID: true` was tried and does not engage on this path, and a chown repair is a see-saw because the mismatch is symmetric between container user and VM user.

The containerized Playwright recipe requires `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` (with `-e HOME=/tmp`): the Playwright image runs as root and /workspaces/mcm is bind-mounted, so every artifact it writes (test-results/, playwright-report/, tests/e2e/web/setup/.auth/user.json) lands root-owned in the working tree and the NEXT invocation dies with EACCES on test-results/.last-run.json, which `coder` cannot even delete. Measured 2026-08-03; `sudo chown -R coder:coder /workspaces/mcm` is the repair, and onCreateCommand self-heals the known artifact paths on container recreate.

Running the containerized Playwright recipe from a worktree fails by going QUIET rather than erroring: only /workspaces/mcm is bind-mounted from the Docker host, so mounting /home/coder/worktrees/<slug> succeeds and yields a near-empty auto-created directory — measured 2026-09-21 as 2 entries where the worktree has 31 — surfacing as `stat node_modules/.bin/playwright: no such file or directory` or as a run that collects zero tests. The workaround is to stage the worktree into a named volume, never to copy it into /workspaces/mcm, which is the shared checkout another session is working in.

The dev-ollama compose file pins its image by tag AND digest (currently ollama/ollama:0.40.11@sha256:dea72d1e…, bumped deliberately rather than floating), declares `restart: unless-stopped` and an `ollama list` healthcheck, and persists models in the `dev-ollama-models` named volume — so models survive container restarts, while a devcontainer rebuild that resets the nested docker storage re-pulls once.

scripts/devcontainer-ollama.sh is deliberately best-effort and idempotent: it exits 0 when the nested dockerd is not ready or the API has not answered within its ~10 s probe loop, so a failed Ollama start can never block container start and agent flows simply fall back to Anthropic. It pulls the model named by DEVCONTAINER_OLLAMA_MODEL (default qwen2.5) once, backgrounded via setsid, because a first-run ~4.7 GB pull must not delay container readiness; the balanced qwen2.5:32b tier is a by-hand pull only because CPU inference makes it slow.

A blocked Ollama egress destination retires merge-gating tiers rather than merely failing a command: the canonical allowlist carries both `registry.ollama.ai` (the manifest host compiled into the ollama binary) and the pinned Cloudflare R2 blob host every model layer is served from (item #394). With either absent, `ollama pull` dies at DNS and `ollama list` stays empty, which makes the golden tier (nx test:golden movie-assistant), the agent half of the E2E gate, and nx up-agents-prod's model precheck unreproducible locally, and makes a real defect indistinguishable from an absent model. The blob host is pinned by exact FQDN instead of `*.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` because the subdomain is Ollama's R2 account id (constant across pulls) and the wildcard would open every account's bucket — so a layer failure after a clean manifest means the account id changed, not a stale ipset.

The `coder` UID renumber belongs in `toolchain.Dockerfile` at user-creation time, not in a layer on top of the prebuilt image: the toolchain image creates `coder` at 1000:1000 and moves the base image's `node` aside to 1100 first, so the container user matches the uid that owns the workspace on the sandbox side, and the overlay copy-up cost is zero because those files do not exist yet. The ownership-repair helper `.devcontainer/fix-workspace-ownership.sh` — which fixes only mismatched entries rather than `chown -R`-ing a large tree on every start — is wired into the sandbox config's lifecycle hooks; the retained Docker Desktop path instead uses the inline `chown` list in its own `onCreateCommand`.

`init-firewall.sh` exposes one deliberate, off-by-default widening lever: `FIREWALL_ALLOW_CDN_RANGES=1` additionally allowlists the published AWS-CloudFront and Cloudflare CIDR ranges (from ip-ranges.amazonaws.com and cloudflare.com/ips-v4) for the case where a CDN round-robins to an address the per-domain A-record snapshot missed. It is off by default precisely because it opens egress to both providers' whole edge networks, so the tight per-domain list remains the default posture and re-applying the script is the first remedy for a stalled pull.

`scripts/gen-egress-policy.mjs` never writes a file: both enforcement forms (`--format sbx-policy` for the host-side sandbox policy and `--format ipset-domains` for `init-firewall.sh`) are piped by their consumer, so there is no generated artifact that can go stale in git and silently disagree with `.devcontainer/egress-allowlist.json`. The forge registry host is never stored in the canonical list — it is injected at runtime via `--forge-host`, and an absent value omits the entry cleanly rather than erroring.

`.devcontainer/verify/verify-firewall-allowlist.sh` does not carry its own copy of the expected destinations — a check holding its own expectation cannot detect drift in the thing it checks. It resolves each canonical domain through `scripts/gen-egress-policy.mjs` and asserts that at least one of its addresses is present in the live `allowed-domains` ipset, which also makes the `cdnRotating: true` class visible as the documented re-apply reflex rather than as a missing rule.

The dev-ollama image pin is maintained rather than decorative: `dev-ollama.compose.yaml` was invisible to Renovate's docker-compose manager (whose default pattern requires the basename to begin with `compose`/`docker-compose`), so the ref sat un-bumped with `docker:pinDigests` already enabled; `renovate.json` now carries a strict superset pattern so the file is seen, and `scripts/__tests__/infra-image-scan.test.mjs` fails the build if any third-party image reference under `infrastructure-as-code/` carries no `@sha256:` digest — making a stale or un-pinned ref a real finding instead of a silent one.

Each destination in `.devcontainer/egress-allowlist.json` carries a `domain`, a `group` drawn from `agent | source | registry | packages | app`, a non-empty `reason` and a boolean `cdnRotating` flag; `scripts/gen-egress-policy.mjs --check` validates the whole file and exits 1 naming the offending entry, rejecting a bare IP, an empty or missing reason, an unknown group, a duplicate domain, a dotless hostname, a topology-sensitive suffix such as `.ts.net`/`.internal`/`.local`, and the forge registry host pasted in while `FORGE_REGISTRY_HOST` is set in the environment. Emission always validates first, so a malformed list is refused rather than piped into a live enforcement layer.

`scripts/gen-egress-policy.mjs` emits both enforcement forms in a deterministic order — by group in the fixed order agent, source, registry, packages, app, then alphabetically by domain, with the `--forge-host` entry appended last so its presence or absence never reorders the rest — which is what makes a regenerated form produce an empty diff.

The canonical allowlist encodes the telemetry inversion as an invariant: its `$mustNeverAppearHere` section forbids the forge/tailnet host, any credential, the OpenWiki analytics host, and every Claude Code / Anthropic telemetry endpoint (`statsig.*` and similar), because telemetry is disabled by configuration rather than permitted by allowlisting. The `wiki-update` Nx target setting `OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` is the enforcement point (the Windows host has no egress firewall as a backstop), and the `containerEnv` entry is defence in depth for an ad-hoc bare `openwiki` call inside the container — so a blocked telemetry host is a working configuration, not a missing allowlist entry.

`.devcontainer/egress-allowlist.json` records its deliberate omissions in `$consideredAndExcluded`, distinct from `$mustNeverAppearHere`: hosts that are permissible but unnecessary, such as Claude Code's self-update host (updates arrive by rebuilding the image), the package/toolchain install hosts `archive.ubuntu.com`, `security.ubuntu.com` and `static.rust-lang.org`, the hosted Nx cache, and third-party aggregators whose primary sources are already listed. The section exists so a later diagnosis can distinguish an intentional absence from a missing rule, and the stated bar for adding an entry is a symptom that requires it.

`.devcontainer/verify/verify-egress-allowlist-contract.sh` is the contract check that keeps the two egress enforcement layers from forking: its eight assertions cover one emitted line per destination in both `sbx-policy` and `ipset-domains` formats, byte-identical and stably ordered output across runs, `--forge-host` appending exactly one entry to each form, omission of `--forge-host` being clean (exit 0, no literal, no stderr), `--check` accepting the committed file, and `--check` rejecting each of a bare IP, an empty reason and an unknown group. Its expected destination count is read from the canonical file rather than hardcoded, and it runs in any mode (Windows host, dev container or sandbox VM) because it only shells out to `node` and reads committed files.

`verify-firewall-allowlist.sh` also derives its per-group reachability probes from `.devcontainer/egress-allowlist.json` (one representative domain per `group` value, read at run time) rather than hardcoding them, so a newly added group cannot be silently left unprobed while the check still reports PASS.

infrastructure-as-code/docker/dev-ollama.compose.yaml is a dev-only helper, deliberately not part of the prod/homelab agent stack: feature 019 removed containerized Ollama from that stack, whose gateway serves via host Ollama. It exists only because nested DinD broke the host-Ollama path (host.docker.internal now resolves to the dev container rather than Windows), and it is brought up solely so heavy agent-flow iteration can run locally instead of on the paid Anthropic API.
